form_note: The right (continuation) sheet of the 1840 schedule. Columns as printed, left to right: twelve SLAVES columns (six male, six female age bands); TOTAL — number of persons in each family; seven NUMBER OF PERSONS IN EACH FAMILY EMPLOYED IN columns (mining, agriculture, commerce, manufactures and trades, navigation of the ocean, navigation of canals lakes and rivers, learned professions and engineers); PENSIONERS FOR REVOLUTIONARY OR MILITARY SERVICES (ages, names); six DEAF AND DUMB, BLIND, AND INSANE WHITE PERSONS columns; four of the same for coloured persons; and seven SCHOOLS, &c. columns. A blank cell on this form is a zero and is recorded as 0.
closure_note: The enumerator added his own totals at the foot of the sheet. Those printed totals are transcribed under `footer_as_read` and are the committed data on this sheet. Where a per-line reading is attempted it is checked against them and its residual recorded; a reading is never adjusted to make a total come out.

stroke_overlap_test.what: the test that settled the six two-stroke figures on this sheet, and the nine figures it is calibrated on. T-0647.
stroke_overlap_test.the_problem: This hand builds BOTH 11 and 4 out of two slanted strokes and nothing else, and every earlier pass argued the difference in prose — 'tops level', 'set below and right', 'the sheet's reference pair'. 33S7-9YYJ-6H says plainly why that failed: 'the pitch test does not separate them on this sheet', because a within-digit stroke spread and a between-digit pitch overlap on that leaf. Neither stroke weight nor stroke height separates them either: 33S7-9YYJ-24's line 21 is a 4 by arithmetic and its two strokes are twins (weight ratio 0.907, height ratio 1.094), exactly like this sheet's line 2.
stroke_overlap_test.the_measure: X OVERLAP of the two strokes' ink bounding boxes — min(x1) − max(x0), in pixels. Positive means the strokes stand over one another in x; negative means one is wholly right of the other. It works because the difference is a fact about the FORM and not about the hand: two digits written side by side occupy two x slots, and one numeral's two strokes share a slot however far their feet drift apart. Measured by tools/census_pair_geometry.py, which imports read_census_continuation's ink mask and component finder rather than defining a second one.
stroke_overlap_test.calibrated_on: NINE figures whose value is fixed by arithmetic — a column or a footing that closes — and not by anyone's eye. Nothing on this sheet is in the calibration set.

The TOTAL column still does not, and it still cannot, because its printed footing is one glyph short of legible. What changed with T-0565 is that the column is now read line by line on a committed index and 105 is arithmetically dead: the sheet's floor is 136 against a footing that would have to be 105.
industry_columns_superseded_note: the pass before this one recorded the two written industry columns provisionally, indexed by image y, with commerce closing at 27 and manufactures standing at 17 against a printed 15. column_closure above replaces that block: manufactures closes at 15 (the y2867 glyph is a 3, not a 5) and the learned professions close at 3. The provisional block is removed rather than kept alongside, so there is one reading of each column on this sheet and not two.

line_index.method: The 22 entry_y values in column_closure (commerce 12, manufactures 9, learned professions 3) are merged where two stand within 30 px — three pairs do, because two industry columns can carry an entry for the same family — and a straight grid y = origin + pitch*n is fitted to what is left, rejecting any fit that puts two anchors on one line and scoring by rms residual. The TOTAL column is not used, which is the whole point: the row index and the numbers are then independent, and a number can be read AGAINST the grid instead of being used to build it.
line_index.jackknife: Refitting with each anchor dropped in turn, 20 of the 22 drops still choose 30 lines. The two that do not are the two END anchors, y658 and y2867: dropping an endpoint shortens the fitted span by a line, so it returns 29 and 28 respectively. No interior anchor carries the result.

line_index.total_column_offset_px: The TOTAL column's glyphs top out about 13 px above the industry columns' on the same line (mean -12.7, sd 7 over the 29 groups the grid places), which is the pen reaching the wider cell first. Residuals in records[] are stated against the raw grid, so subtract 13 to read them as departures from the column's own trend.

unassigned_ink.what: one stroke, tapered, with a heavy foot — the shape of every 1 on this sheet
unassigned_ink.why_unassigned: the grid has 30 lines and the TOTAL column has 31 glyph groups, and this is the surplus. It stands 39 px below line 28 (which g28 already occupies at a residual of -5) and 37 px above line 29 (which g30 occupies at +4) — dead centre between two numbers that are each where the grid puts them. It cannot be line 28's second digit: it is to the LEFT of g28 (x1411-1430 against x1433-1458) and this hand's second digit is always to the right. It cannot be part of line 29's number: g30 is already a complete two-glyph number and this stands above it, not beside it.
